$description: Geslaagd Momentum tokens in the W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) format. This is the single source of truth for the focused-momentum learning product: white and violet surfaces, ink text, and a restrained violet primary with blue/amber/red chart accents. A forest/emerald dark palette also exists (below) but no surface currently opts into it. Edit values here only -- generated CSS and portable tokens are outputs.

background.$description: Quiet near-white surface for reading and forms.

foreground.$description: Ink text with a violet undertone.

primary.$description: Momentum violet. Drives the one obvious action, progress, and trusted links.

mutedForeground.$description: Darkened past the WCAG-AA minimum on purpose: this text runs as small as 12px (meta/label steps) across badges and captions, where a ratio just over 4.5:1 still reads as low-contrast.

accent.$description: Soft violet wash for selected states and moments of discovery.

background.$description: Deep ink and forest base for concentrated study.

foreground.$description: Warm ivory text, never stark white.

primary.$description: Luminous emerald for the next step and verified progress.

accent.$description: Aurora violet for selected states and moments of discovery.

sans.$description: Interface and body typeface: direct, warm, and easy to scan.

serif.$description: Display typeface for confident learning moments and outcome-led headlines.

mono.$description: Reserved for source, provenance, step, and system metadata.

scale.$description: The semantic type ramp. Each step names a role, not a size, so hierarchy stays consistent across every surface. Generated into --text-<step>-* custom properties and matching .type-<step> utility classes.

display.$description: Marketing hero and the single biggest statement on a page. At most once per screen.

heading1.$description: Page title. The answer to 'where am I'. Restrained on purpose: in a workspace the title orients you, it does not announce itself.

bodyLong.$description: Sustained reading: chapter summaries and explanations. Larger and airier than interface text on purpose.

label.$description: Form labels, buttons, badges, table headers.

meta.$description: Source, provenance, IDs, timestamps, log lines. The only place mono appears.

density.$description: Two spacing scales, split by role rather than by page. Comfortable is the :root default and belongs to content people read; .density-compact is the chrome scale for sidebars, toolbars and dense lists, and lands a single-line row near 32px. Use these values directly -- multiplying them in a calc() defeats the point of having a scale.

blockGap.$description: Gap inside a section or card.

rowPaddingY.$description: A single list/table row -- sidebar items, log lines.

cardPaddingY.$description: A standalone content card or panel -- more room than a row, without inventing a one-off multiplier at each call site.

base.$description: Soft, intentional corners; enough warmth without making the product playful.
A four-pixel rhythm that supports generous breathing room.

elevation.$description: Depth is carried by hairlines and surface layering, not by drop shadow. These two steps are only for things that genuinely float above the page -- menus, dialogs, the command palette. A card that merely sits on the page gets a border, not a shadow.

soft.$description: Menus, popovers and dropdowns: close to the surface they came from.

lift.$description: Dialogs, sheets and the command palette, which take over the screen.

soft.$description: Menus and popovers. On deep ink the shadow reads as depth without a lit edge.

lift.$description: Dialogs, sheets and the command palette.

standard.$description: The calm, decisive motion curve for Momentum feedback.
